About | I-Corps South Skip to main content Main navigation Home About Leadership Programs About Programs NSF I-Corps Program Regional I-Corps Courses Local I-Corps Courses Accelerate Program Get Involved I-Corps Mentor Network I-Corps Instructor Training Events News Resources Southeast Region I-Corps Hub: Goals and Mission The Southeast Region I-Corps Hub is committed to transforming the university innovation process, empowering researchers, and fostering a robust regional and national ecosystem for technological advancement and commercialization View All Programs Who We Are The staff and instructors of the NSF I-Corps Hub: Southeast Region are passionate about empowering academic researchers with the knowledge and skills needed to excel in innovation and entrepreneurship. Our mission is to guide researchers in transforming their discoveries into impactful solutions for society. Goals Reimagine University Innovation: Enhance regional and national competitiveness by rethinking the journey from research ideation to invention to spinout. Leverage leadership in science to drive impactful innovation. Develop Tomorrow’s Technical Leaders: Equip researchers, faculty, and students with the entrepreneurial mindset, skills, and networks they need to pursue meaningful career paths. Transforming Traditional University Research The Hub fosters a fundamental shift in how universities
Faculty, students, and staff are encouraged to engage directly with stakeholders and potential users of their technologies.

From ideation to de-risking and funding support , our nationally recognized instructors, trainers, and mentors provide seamless guidance to help participants transition their ideas from lab to market efficiently and effectively.
Together, this network advances innovation education to meet America’s need for cutting-edge technological development.

Teams I-Corps Teams are composed of academic researchers, student entrepreneurs, and business mentors¬ who participate in the curriculum via online instruction and onsite activities through Partners and Hubs.

Partners I-Corps™ Partners are top universities that provide infrastructure, resources, mentorship, networking opportunities, and funding to enable teams to transition their work into the marketplace or into becoming I-Corps Team applicants.

Hubs I-Corps Hubs support regional needs for innovation education and work to build, utilize, and sustain a national innovation ecosystem that further enhances the development of technologies that benefit society.
This network collaborates to address America’s growing need for innovation education.
Through collaboration and education, the Southeast Region I-Corps Hub is empowering innovators to create impactful solutions and drive America’s future forward.
Supported by NSF Award 2430380.

Programs | I-Corps South Skip to main content Main navigation Home About Leadership Programs About Programs NSF I-Corps Program Regional I-Corps Courses Local I-Corps Courses Accelerate Program Get Involved I-Corps Mentor Network I-Corps Instructor Training Events News Resources Programs NSF I-Corps Program The National Science Foundation Innovation Corps (I-Corps™) program equips scientists and engineers with the tools to extend their research beyond the laboratory and accelerate the commercialization of cutting-edge, NSF-funded innovations. By engaging extensively with potential customers, teams validate the real-world applications of their technology and avoid creating solutions that lack market demand—a key reason for startup failure. The immersive 7-week curriculum combines online instruction with on-site activities, challenging teams to conduct at least 15 customer interviews per week. By the end of the program, each team will have connected with over 100 potential customers, gaining invaluable insights to guide their commercialization journey. The workshops will help PhD students, Postdocs, and Faculty members at universities adopt an entrepreneurial mindset to question how they ultimately hope their research and careers will make an impact. Unlike the Local, Regional, and National I-Corps programs, participants in Pathways to Impact workshops are not expected to have a technology commercialization idea in mind. Apply Now Program Benefits Provide participants with a new framework to view their research goals. Expose participants to the entrepreneurial mindset, and how it can help guide their research and career. Inspire researchers to explore–through outside stakeholders and their own community–how their research/discoveries might be implemented for societal impact. Provide a set of tools to shape participants’ research objectives to be more use-inspired and impactful. Reduce psychological barriers
Supported by NSF Award 2430380.

I-Corps Instructor Training | I-Corps South Skip to main content Main navigation Home About Leadership Programs About Programs NSF I-Corps Program Regional I-Corps Courses Local I-Corps Courses Accelerate Program Get Involved I-Corps Mentor Network I-Corps Instructor Training Events News Resources I-Corps Instructor Training The Southeast I-Corps Hub is dedicated to fostering the next generation of I-Corps instructors to deliver impactful, evidence-based entrepreneurship programs. These programs drive economic development and commercialization at undergraduate, graduate and faculty levels, helping transform innovative ideas and research into real-world solutions. With the success of the National Science Foundation’s I-Corps program, universities nationwide are adopting this proven methodology. To support these efforts, the Southeast I-Corps Hub provides comprehensive instructor training to equip emerging instructors with the skills and knowledge needed to deliver high-quality I-Corps programs. Find more details about our I-Corps instructor training and development pathways below. Southeast Regional Instructor Academy TRAINING OVERVIEW: The Regional Instructor Academy is designed to share: methodologies and instructor strategies for success, tactical classroom management techniques, and other tools to successfully host an evidence-based entrepreneurship (EBE) course. These

Opportunities for Advanced Instructors OVERVIEW: We welcome continued engagement from experienced instructors joining Regional Hub or National I-Corps Mentoring Networks and have further opportunities available to them to support continued development and positioning within the national I-Corps ecosystem.

Additionally, I-Corps Offers ongoing growth opportunities for more advanced instructors, including nominated selection to become a National Instructor through I-Corps' competitive and formal Faculty-in-Training (FIT) program.
Supported by NSF Award 2430380.

These courses emphasize the importance of conducting effective customer discovery interviews—an essential first step in the commercialization process. Designed to build entrepreneurial skills, these courses are beneficial for anyone, regardless of their career path. Local I-Corps programs are typically hosted at individual universities and are often open to participants from outside the university community. Build Innovation Skills: Gain, practice, and refine entrepreneurial techniques. Increase Commercial Success: Improve your chances of successfully bringing your innovation to market. Expand Your Network: Connect with peers, instructors, investors, customers, and mentors who share your entrepreneurial interests.

Regional I-Corps Courses | I-Corps South Skip to main content Main navigation Home About Leadership Programs About Programs NSF I-Corps Program Regional I-Corps Courses Local I-Corps Courses Accelerate Program Get Involved I-Corps Mentor Network I-Corps Instructor Training Events News Resources Regional I-Corp Courses Regional I-Corps courses are designed to help faculty, researchers, and graduate students assess the commercial viability of their technology-based innovations. Using the Lean LaunchPad methodology (also known as Lean Startup), participants systematically test key assumptions about their innovations and identify customer problems their technology can solve better than current alternatives. This process, known as finding “technology-problem fit,” is a critical first step toward commercial success for any technology venture. Through this program, participants: Learn and apply customer discovery techniques to gain a deeper understanding of their ecosystem and stakeholders. Receive guidance from trained instructors and mentors to identify key milestones and chart a commercialization pathway. Connect with like-minded innovators across the Southeast, fostering collaboration and idea exchange. Apply Now Program Benefits Participants in the Regional I-Corps program gain access to valuable resources and opportunities, including: Market Insights: Obtain critical feedback
Networking and Mentorship: Build connections and receive mentorship from experienced industry experts, entrepreneurs, and innovators.
Entrepreneurial Skills: Develop the mindset and toolset necessary for success in academia, industry, startups, or government careers.
Eligibility Requirements Regional I-Corps courses are open to: Faculty, researchers, and students with technology-based innovation ideas or Intellectual Property (IP).
Supported by NSF Award 2430380.
